ACCEPTI accept the selected-union both-far compensation theorem and the repaired arbitrary-far E-frontier dependency under the stated hypotheses.I did not execute the verifier or Lean. This verdict is based on the supplied source constructor, the written all-parameter arguments, and the repaired support and separation proofs. The reported controls are supplementary evidence only.1. The earlier  $+2$  source-charge objection was mistakenThe earlier objection incorrectly placed the two R bar-end supports inside R’s endpoint-tile footprint.For
$$R=U(L,10,f),\qquad
\operatorname{chart}(r,c)=(a-11+r,C+1-c),$$
the two bar-end supports at intrinsic coordinates  $(0,0)$  and  $(0,L+1)$  map to columns  $C+1$  and  $C-L$ . The endpoint bar occupies columns from
$$F=C+1-L$$
through  $C$ . Since  $F$  is even and  $C$  is odd, those two supports lie in the immediately adjacent physical tile columns outside the entire endpoint-tile footprint. They are not merely outside the bar cells; they are outside every endpoint tile.The complete R count is therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{matching}(R)&=L+4+\frac f2,\\
\operatorname{endpointTiles}(R)&=\frac L2+5+\frac f2,\\
\operatorname{supportsInside}(R)&=
4+\left(\frac f2-1\right)+2
=5+\frac f2.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\operatorname{charge}(R)
=
\left(L+4+\frac f2\right)
+\left(5+\frac f2\right)
-2\left(\frac L2+5+\frac f2\right)
=-1.$$
This gives, for example,
$$(71,45,18)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 71+18-2\cdot45=-1$$
for  $R=U(54,10,26)$ , and
$$(65,41,16)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 65+16-2\cdot41=-1$$
for the sharp E witness  $U(50,10,22)$ .The repaired T count is also correct. For
$$T=U(M,4,g),\qquad
\operatorname{chart}(r,c)=(a-8+r,s+1-c),$$
the complete inside-support set consists of:both bar-end supports;the two near lateral supports at intrinsic even rows  $2,4$ ;the far lateral supports at intrinsic even rows  $2,4,\ldots,g$ .The two axial terminal supports at intrinsic rows  $5$  and  $g+1$  lie in the next physical tile rows beyond the corresponding terminal endpoints and are outside the endpoint-tile footprint. Thus
$$\operatorname{supportsInside}(T)
=
2+2+\frac g2
=
4+\frac g2.$$
With
$$\operatorname{matching}(T)=M+1+\frac g2,\qquad
\operatorname{endpointTiles}(T)=M+2+\frac g2,$$
we obtain
$$\operatorname{charge}(T)
=
\left(M+1+\frac g2\right)
+\left(4+\frac g2\right)
-2\left(M+2+\frac g2\right)
=1-M.$$
The explicit example
$$T=U(28,4,24)$$
therefore has
$$(41,42,16)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
41+16-2\cdot42=-27,$$
as claimed. Consequently the pair’s negative mass is exactly
$$1+(M-1)=M,$$
with no positive-owner contribution. The retained mass assertions and the gain ledger are correct.The strengthened comparison of the complete immutable inside-support sets addresses the relevant proof obligation, rather than merely checking aggregate counts.2. The repaired earlier-owner separation closes the previous wording gapThe earlier objection that “all earlier blocks lie to the right” was too broad. The replacement partition is sufficient and correct.For an internal index  $i$ , write
$$C_i=s_i+w_i+13=s_{i-1}+1.$$
Since  $C_i$  is odd, the R endpoints have maximum column  $C_i$ , while the earlier base originals  $B_j$ , including their unbounded long stems, have minimum column at least
$$s_j+2\ge s_{i-1}+2=C_i+1.$$
Thus the base originals and R lie in different physical tile columns. The same column argument applies to the root, whose minimum endpoint column is at least  $C_i+1$ , independently of its breadth.The earlier repair originals  $P_j$ , west rotors  $Z_j$ , and south U originals  $X_j$  need not lie to the right. Their maximum endpoint rows are bounded by
$$a_j+2,\qquad a_j-1,\qquad a_j+2,$$
respectively. Since  $a_i-a_j\ge18$  for  $j<i$ , all of these rows are at most
$$a_i-16,$$
whereas R begins at row  $a_i-11$ . Their physical tile rows are therefore strictly above R’s endpoint tiles, even if their columns overlap R’s horizontal range.This is an exhaustive partition of the earlier H3 records:all earlier base originals;all earlier repairs;all earlier west rotors;all earlier south U originals;the root.It handles arbitrary earlier long-stem depth and leaves no earlier-owner separation gap.The far strip itself is separately covered by the minimum-column bound  $s_j-4$ , while the fixed R bar and near leg use the repaired column/row partition. Thus the earlier-column issue is resolved without introducing a depth cutoff.3. The arbitrary-far E frontier is now an all-parameter argumentThe E-frontier table remains valid for arbitrary even  $f\ge4$ . For the first later block  $k$  with
$$F\ge s_k-4,$$
parity gives
$$s_k-4\le F\le s_{k-1}-6.$$
The four possible phases are exhaustive:
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c}
F & \text{legal terminal bound} & d\\
\hline
s_k-4 & b\le a_k-3 & 0\\
s_k-2 & b\le a_k-3 & 1\text{ only at }b=a_k-3\\
s_k & b\le a_k-5 & 2\text{ only at }b=a_k-7,a_k-5\\
s_k+2\text{ through }s_{k-1}-6
& b\le a_k-9
& 1\text{ only at }b=a_k-9
\end{array}$$
The displayed first old endpoint in each phase is the correct obstruction: $X_k$  at  $F=s_k-4$ ; $Z_k$  at  $F=s_k-2$ ; $Z_k$ , with the P far stem in the partner column, at  $F=s_k$ ;the P bar at  $F\ge s_k+2$ .The legal terminal bounds stop R before any later block can contribute: every block after  $k$  begins at row at least
$$a_{k+1}-8\ge a_k+10,$$
while all legal R terminals satisfy  $b\le a_k-3$ . If no  $k$  exists, column separation handles arbitrary  $f$ .The exact receipts also remain consistent:the  $F=s_k-2$  phase gives one full tile and three events, debit  $-1$ ;the  $F=s_k$  phase gives the  $h$ -dependent two-way receipt, debit  $-2$ ;the P-bar phase gives one event, debit  $-1$ ;the  $F=s_k-4$  phase has no separate R far receipt.Together with the corrected R charge, this proves
$$\Delta\Phi(R\mid H3)=1-d$$
for the entire unbounded even-f family.The old left-chain theorem supplies
$$\Delta\Phi(T\mid H3)=M-1-\delta$$
for arbitrary even  $g\ge4$ . Its exceptional  $\delta=1$  phase forces
$$M=s_i-s_k+4\ge28.$$
Thus the new E dependency is not relying on finite catalogue exhaustion or finite depth checks.4. The pair ledger, nonstacking, and triple correction are consistentFor  $q\ge2$ , the R and T far stems lie in distinct physical tile columns.For  $q=0$ ,
$$G=F+1.$$
The mutual directed events occur at the even rows in the common far-stem range. The mutual full tiles occur one tile-row below the corresponding event rows. Because  $b$  is even and  $y$  is odd,
$$|A|-|B|=[b<y]=\epsilon,$$
so the mutual signed contribution is exactly
$$-2\epsilon.$$
The deductions cannot stack. In every positive-deduction  $q=0$  phase, the coupled T frontier forces  $y<b$ , hence  $\epsilon=0$ . Therefore
$$d+2\epsilon\le2.$$
This is the key inequality needed for the lower bound.The  $\chi$  term is also correctly isolated. When
$$q=0,\qquad
F=s_k-4,\qquad
b=a_k-3,\qquad
y\ge a_k-2,$$
the tile with top-left coordinate  $(a_k-3,F)$  has:R at its upper-left cell;T in both right cells;the old X endpoint in its lower-left cell.That is a new three-owner full tile, contributing  $+2$ . The X-to-T directed event in the lower row is already part of the exceptional old T-frontier receipt when that phase is active; it is not an additional unaccounted event. The R/X vertical directions are excluded by the relevant immutable axial supports, and the R/T upper-row directions are exactly the mutual pair events. Therefore the only additional correction is precisely  $+2\chi$ .The exact one-pair identity is consequently
$$\Delta\Phi_i
=
M_i-d_i-\delta_i-2\epsilon_i+2\chi_i.$$
Since
$$d_i+2\epsilon_i\le2,\qquad M_i\ge6,$$
we have, when  $\delta_i=0$ ,
$$\Delta\Phi_i\ge M_i-2\ge4.$$
When  $\delta_i=1$ , the exceptional frontier forces  $M_i\ge28$ , giving
$$\Delta\Phi_i\ge M_i-3\ge25.$$
Therefore every selected pair contributes at least four units, and
$$\Delta\Phi
=
\sum_{i\in J}
\left(M_i-d_i-\delta_i-2\epsilon_i+2\chi_i\right)
\ge4|J|.$$
5. Automatic disjointness of full endpoint-tile footprintsThe aligned R bar gives the necessary envelope for the entire pair.For pair  $j$ ,
$$F_j=G_j-1-q_j\le G_j-1,
\qquad
s_j+1<C_j.$$
Hence every endpoint column of  $T_j$ , including its bar, near leg, and arbitrary far leg, lies inside the physical tile-column interval covered by the aligned R-bar columns  $[F_j,C_j]$ . R itself is obviously inside that interval.Now take selected pairs  $i<j$ . The nonfar endpoints of pair  $i$  end at row at most  $a_i-1$ , while
$$a_j-11\ge a_i+7.$$
Only an arbitrary far stem of pair  $i$  could reach pair  $j$ ’s vertical range.Suppose such a stem column  $x$  meets pair  $j$ ’s footprint. By the aligned-bar envelope, its physical tile column also meets the R-j bar, so
$$F_j\le x\le C_j.$$
The R-j bar contains an endpoint at every such column on its first bar row  $a_j-11$ . If the earlier stem terminal  $t$  satisfied
$$t\ge a_j-11,$$
the earlier and later originals would share an endpoint, contradicting the assumed endpoint-disjointness of the selected originals.Therefore
$$t<a_j-11.$$
The barrier  $a_j-11$  is even. The R far terminal is even, and the T far terminal is odd. Consequently, this strict inequality places the earlier stem’s endpoint tiles strictly above the later pair’s first bar tile row in both parity cases. If the tile columns do not meet, separation is immediate; if they do meet, the row argument separates them.Thus every two selected pairs have disjoint full endpoint-tile footprints, with no ordering by widths, nesting assumption, support closure, or far-depth cutoff.Since every newly created mixed full tile and every newly created directed event contains at least one new endpoint, all new receipt sets lie inside these pair footprints. The footprints are disjoint, so the one-pair receipts form a disjoint union. Immutable original supports prevent re-crediting old support resources, and owner-labelled events prevent event identity collisions.Scope of this acceptanceThis ACCEPT covers:the simultaneous selected-union theorem;arbitrary even  $f_i,g_i\ge4$ ;the corrected R and T source charges;the repaired arbitrary-f E-frontier dependency;the  $d+2\epsilon\le2$  nonstacking argument;the  $+2\chi$  triple-owner full-tile correction;automatic disjointness of complete pair endpoint-tile footprints;exact set nonreuse and the resulting gain sum.It does not extend to complete-extension existence, arbitrary extra-owner monotonicity, catalogue exhaustion, deeper E incident legs, later return-debit or sharpness results, the global  $5/6$  bound, or rectangular-grid triple equality.
